title: Hyperparameterized Savings Initiative: Roadmap, OKRs, and Sprint Cadence
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: This initiative treats cost optimizations (batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization, request shaping) as a small but high-leverage hyperparameter search problem across production workloads. Instead of one-off ad-hoc experiments, we will build a repeatable roadmap and cadence for hypothesis-driven tuning: an experiment grid, canary pilot patterns, measurement dashboards, and automated rollout gates that tie back to OKRs.

Background and motivation: We have many isolated wins from batching tweaks, cache TTL changes, and quantization profiles, but they are difficult to reproduce across workloads and maintenance is ad hoc. This initiative aims to: (1) formalize a canonical set of tuning axes and default-safe profiles, (2) create an experiment harness that safely compares configurations on live traffic with minimal customer risk, and (3) operationalize progression from experiment -> pilot -> platform default with observable rollback gates.

Hypothesis: By treating serving knobs as composable hyperparameters and standardizing an experiment/rollout playbook, we can lower per-token compute cost by 12-20% across the average customer workload within one quarter while keeping P95 latency regressions under 3% and reducing manual tuning cycles by >50%.

Objectives and key results (OKRs):
- OKR 1 (Savings): Reduce weighted per-token GPU cost by 15% for the top-30% of active tenants (by spend) by 2026-06-30.
- OKR 2 (Reliability): Maintain 99.95% availability for impacted endpoints during pilots and keep P95 latency regression <3% vs baseline.
- OKR 3 (Velocity): Establish a documented experiment grid and release cadence that reduces time-to-decision from experiment to pilot from median 6 weeks to <=2 weeks.

Roadmap & milestones:
- Feb (Discovery): Workload stratification, select initial 12 tenants for pilot, define tuning axes and safety constraints.
- Mar (Experiment grid & harness): Implement experiment harness that can run parallel A/B/C tests across knobs (batch thresholds, cache TTLs, quant profiles) and surface statistical significance.
- Apr (Controlled pilots): Run canary pilots on the 12 tenants with tight rollback triggers; collect cost and latency metrics and human post-mortems.
- May (Platform defaults): Propose 3 platform profiles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) backed by experiment data and create rollout automation.
- Jun (Rollout & OKR evaluation): Rollout conservative profile to 25% of eligible non-enterprise tenants, monitor, and evaluate OKR progress.

Measurement plan and success metrics:
- Primary metric: weighted-per-token GPU compute cost (normalized to runtime-1.18 baseline).
- Safety metrics: P95 latency change, 99th percentile error spikes, percentage of requests hitting model fallbacks.
- Quality guardrails: embedding similarity drift (where applicable), token-level output divergence sampling against control prompts.
- Business metrics: monthly cost savings in dollars, net effect on billable token throughput, and any observed churn signals.

Experiment design / technical approach:
- Treat knobs as vectorized hyperparameters (batch_size_threshold, prefer_cached_prefix, kv_cache_ttl_seconds, quant_profile_id, request_shaping_policy).
- Use traffic shadowing + small-traffic A/B splits for experiments where possible; spike testing in staging for extreme aggressive profiles.
- Implement per-tenant experiment metadata tagging, per-tenant rollback buckets, and a scheduled decision checkpoint (72-hour min) for human review.

Rollout & automation:
- Canary policy: 1% -> 5% -> 25% staged progression with automatic rollback if safety triggers fire.
- Rollout gating: automated checks run at 1h, 6h, 24h intervals; if any safety metric crosses threshold we auto-roll back and page on-call.
- Platform integration: expose profiles via Console and API; allow Dedicated customers to opt-in/out of platform defaults.

Cross-functional owners and communication:
- PM (owner): Aisha Patel (initiative lead)
- Engineering leads: Marco Chen (runtime & orchestration), Deepa Rao (monitoring & rollout automation)
- Research/Applied ML: Leah Kim (quantization validation, evals)
- Design/Console: Jonah Park (UX for profile selection + alerts)
- SRE/Support: Priya Menon (on-call runbooks)

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Quantization introduces subtle quality regressions for edge prompts. Mitigation: require per-model quality checks and a small adversarial prompt set in the experiment.
- Risk: Batch tuning increases tail latency on low-throughput tenants. Mitigation: per-tenant thresholds and flow-control heuristics; conservative profile as default.
- Risk: Operational complexity increases maintenance burden. Mitigation: automate decision gates and document runbooks; collapse common successful combos into named profiles.

Outcomes & acceptance criteria:
- Acceptance: Achieve >=12% measured weighted per-token compute cost reduction on pilot tenants with P95 latency regression <3% and no customer-facing errors attributable to the changes.
- Deliverables: experiment harness (internal repo + docs), dashboard with per-tenant cost/latency views, three platform profiles, rollout automation and runbook, PRD and post-mortem template.

Why this is different: Instead of treating batching, caching, and quantization as separate projects, this initiative creates a composable lifecycle that treats knobs as parameters to be searched and promoted, enabling reproducible savings across customers and faster iteration on trade-offs.
updates: 2026-02-18: Initiative created and prioritized in PM backlog. Kickoff scheduled.
2026-02-23: Kickoff with Eng/Research/Console. Agreed on initial tuning axes and selection criteria for pilot tenants.
2026-03-03: Experiment grid design documented and reviewed. Leah provided quant validation checklist; Deepa outlined monitoring hooks required for gating.
2026-03-08: ENG spike complete: prototype harness can run 3-parallel configs with per-tenant tagging in staging. Baseline runtime runs captured (runtime-1.18).
2026-03-12: Decided to split profiles into conservative/balanced/aggressive. Created draft rollout canary plan and rollback thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: >=12% weighted per-token compute cost reduction on pilot tenants vs baseline
P95 latency regression <3% for all pilot tenants during 72h observation windows
No increase in high-severity customer errors attributable to changes
Documentation: PRD + runbooks + dashboard operational by pilot start
Automation: Canary progression and rollback automation configured and tested in staging
risks: Quantization quality regressions on adversarial prompts
Tail latency increases for small tenants with larger batch thresholds
Complexity of many small experiments creating operational debt
Potential lack of statistically significant signal for low-traffic tenants
notes: Next immediate tasks: finalize experiment grid CSV, onboard 12 pilot tenants, and clear monitoring hooks with Deepa. Schedule a 1-hour cross-functional review after first 72h pilot window.
